chunks.title: Neuroflux: the complete user guide
chunks.text:
**Make the visuals move. Mix the camera in. Capture a take worth keeping.**

A practical, plain-English manual for the current Neuroflux Visual Rig. Covers the live rig, all 110 core controls, camera mixing, sensors, 3D, AI tools, recording, audio routing, editing, exports and sharing.

**Edition:** 23 October 2026. Includes independent Camera FX, Silence Stop, portable whole-app setups, guided walkthroughs and the offline-cache update recovery page. The default values in this guide mean a clean first-run setup; your saved settings or a loaded preset can be different.

**Open the app:** [neuroflux-rig.vercel.app](https://neuroflux-rig.vercel.app/). If a phone acts as though an update never happened, use [Load the latest version](https://neuroflux-rig.vercel.app/update.html), then tap **UPDATE AND OPEN NEUROFLUX**. It refreshes app files while keeping saved recordings and settings. Finish active recordings and exports first.

chunks.title: 1. What this app is doing
chunks.text:
Neuroflux is a visual instrument. Pick a source of sound, choose a visual world, then shape how that world reacts. You can play it gently like a moving backdrop or push it like a live VJ performance.

Think in four layers:

1. **The source:** a loaded track, the built-in demo, a live mic/interface, desktop tab audio where supported, or the silent simulated signal.
2. **The visual:** one of nine engines, shaped with FORM and MOTION, colored with COLOR, and styled with FX.
3. **The performers:** audio reactivity, camera, your fingers, phone sensors, hand tracking and the director can all push the look.
4. **The take:** the recorder builds a separate output picture and audio mix, then saves it on your device.

chunks.title: 1. What this app is doing
chunks.text:
That fourth layer matters. What you see while operating the app and what you put in a saved video do not have to be identical. You can keep a menu open while tweaking and still record a clean picture.

The current app records, exports and hands files to your device's share sheet. It does **not** broadcast your visuals to RTMP/stream URLs or publish directly to social accounts. Platform presets are framing shortcuts. The word STREAM in the lyrics tool means live speech transcription, not a YouTube/Twitch broadcast.

chunks.title: 2. Your first good-looking minute
chunks.text:
1. Open Neuroflux in a normal browser tab. If the app asks how to start, choose **DEMO** for real built-in sound or **SILENT** to start with motion paused; press Play when you want silent simulated motion. You can also choose **FILE** or **MIC / BT**.
2. Open the bottom-right **Menu** button. On a phone the controls rise in a sheet; on a wide screen they sit to the side. The tab strip scrolls sideways, so swipe it to find more pages.
3. Open **SCENES** and load a factory scene such as **OUTRUN**, **LIQUID SUN** or **DMT GATE**. This gives you a coordinated starting look.
4. Open **FX**. Keep FEEDBACK roughly 60–80% and BLOOM around 30–60% while you get a feel for the image. These are starting suggestions, not hard rules.
5. Open **REACT**. Leave INPUT GAIN near 1–1.2× and try BASS › ZOOM around 20%. Listen to a few kicks before making the next change.
6. Move just one control at a time. If the image gets lost, lower FEEDBACK, BLOOM and EXPOSURE before changing ten other things.
7. To keep this look, go to **SCENES → MEMORY BANKS** and hold **A**, **B**, **C** or **D** for about half a second. Holding an occupied slot replaces its saved look.

chunks.title: 2. Your first good-looking minute
chunks.text:
For a first recording, choose **RECORD → OUTPUT**, start with one 720p/30 output and **Clean**, then tap **REC**. Preparation and the output test happen first; a visible **3–2–1** happens just before the take begins. Tap the red stop control to save. Open **RECORD → LIBRARY** to play and download the take.

**Important:** the keyboard shortcut **R means Randomize**, not Record. The REC button is your recording control.

chunks.title: The bottom dock
chunks.text:
| Item | What it is for |
|---|---|
| Source button / SIM, DEMO, FILE, MIC or SYS chip | Opens the source chooser. **INPUT DEVICES** takes you to device selection. **SILENT** returns to simulated analysis without actual sound. |
| Track/status strip | Shows the current source or track and a progress/scrub strip where there is room. Scrub a loaded file to seek; the demo scrub strip jumps through its generated arrangement. It is not a playlist editor. |
| Large Play/Pause button | Controls the current source. For a live mic/system source, pausing releases that input. In silent SIM mode, Play/Pause explicitly runs or pauses the silent simulation. It starts paused. It does not pause a recording. |
| Sparkle / AI button | Tap for the text prompt panel; hold to speak a short visual instruction. |
| REC | Starts a take using saved recording settings. During preparation it can cancel; during recording it becomes a red Stop/Save control with elapsed time. |
| Recorder Pause/Resume | Appears next to REC while a take is running. It pauses the take, not the music or camera. |
| Menu grid / close icon | Opens or closes the native control sheet. |

chunks.title: The bottom dock
chunks.text: On a very narrow phone, track information can shrink or disappear while recording so Stop, Pause and Menu still fit. The controls have not been removed from your recording options.

chunks.title: The top and the little badges
chunks.text:
The scene name/number tells you which engine is active; tap it to go to SCENES. The colored **B / M / H** meters show analyzed bass, mid and high energy. The BPM reactor shows the app's estimate of the pulse; tap it for REACT. Badges such as MIC, CAM, HANDS or DIR show active features and take you to the relevant page when tapped.

BPM is estimated, not a metronome setting. Silent simulation uses a synthetic 120 BPM signal; the demo's arrangement is 124 BPM. Detection can settle on a related half/double-time pulse with real music.

chunks.title: The menu map
chunks.text:
| Page | Use it when you want to… |
|---|---|
| QUICK | Pick an engine, reach performance commands, and use your pinned controls. |
| RECORD | Set up the take, output framing, recording audio and local library. |
| AI | Type/speak a look, run the director, track hands, or show lyrics. |
| SCENES | Pick engines, load factory scenes, save/recall four look slots. |
| INPUT | Choose what the rig hears and which live input device to use. |
| SENSE | Use touch, tilt, gyro, shake, heading or available light information. |
| CAMERA | Choose a camera and blend it with the visual. |
| 3D | Enable camera depth or load a scan file. |
| FORM | Shape the active visual engine. |
| MOTION | Set time, travel, spin, origin and automatic drifting. |
| COLOR | Choose a palette and grade the picture. |
| FX | Add trails, glow, lens distortion and texture. |
| REACT | Decide how sound and detected beats move the picture. |
| SYSTEM | Adjust operator quality/UI, telemetry, wake behavior and app updates. |

chunks.title: Dragging, resetting and pinning
chunks.text:
- **Knobs:** drag up or right to increase; down or left to decrease. Think “slide the value,” not “trace a perfect circle.” A diagonal drag combines the two directions.
- **Faders:** drag to change the level. Their value is still just a control amount; a fader is not automatically an audio volume control.
- **Double-tap a knob/fader:** returns that control to its built-in default. This can differ from the value in the preset you just loaded.
- **Choice rows:** use their left/right arrows, tap the value area to cycle, or drag sideways. Examples are BLEND, PALETTE and SYMMETRY. Do not assume every choice row uses the knob double-tap behavior.
- **Switch rows:** tap to toggle. Keyboard Enter/Space also works when the switch has focus.
- **Hold ordinary knobs/choice/switch rows:** pins or unpins that control in QUICK, roughly a half-second hold. Primary power cards use their own switch behavior rather than every one supporting pinning.
- **ORIGIN XY pad:** drag within the pad to set both axes. Double-tap to center it.
- **Scrolling:** scroll the menu body between groups; swipe the tab strip sideways for hidden tabs. On a phone, the sheet handle lets you change its open position. On a wide screen the sheet uses a side layout.

chunks.title: Gestures on the art itself
chunks.text:
Touch the exposed canvas to use TOUCH FX. With TOUCH FX on, a **two-finger swipe left** goes to the next engine and a right swipe goes to the previous one. With TOUCH FX off, a quick horizontal single-finger swipe can do that job instead. Double-tap the canvas to hide/show the operator interface. These gestures belong on the art, not on a dial or menu row.

**HIDE UI** removes the operator controls; it is separate from recorded Menu visibility. Use the small reveal control, double-tap the canvas, or press H to bring the interface back. Fullscreen is offered only where the browser supports the requested fullscreen API.

chunks.title: 4. How to mix without turning it into soup
chunks.text:
A good mix usually has a clear main idea. Choose one: a tunnel you travel through, a person with graphics around them, a crisp symmetrical pattern, or a soft moving color field. Then let the other controls support that idea.

A reliable order is **engine → form → motion → color → trails/glow → audio response → camera/other performers → recording preview**. You can work in a different order, but changing everything at once makes it hard to know what helped.

Start from a readable image. Turn off AUTOPILOT, AI DIRECTOR and BEAT JUMP while learning a look. If hands or sensors are on, they can add movement too. Bring FEEDBACK and BLOOM down, keep EXPOSURE near 1×, and get FORM where you like it. Then add one effect at a time.

chunks.title: 4. How to mix without turning it into soup
chunks.text:
**Feedback is the picture remembering itself.** With a lot of memory, small zoom/spin/color changes repeat and build up. That is why a tiny TRAIL SPIN can produce an enormous spiral. If the image has become a bright smear, drop FEEDBACK to 0 briefly, then raise it more gently.

**Base amounts and modulation add up.** A low base CHROMA does not guarantee no color separation if HIGH › CHROMA or the director is adding more. A steady TIME dial does not guarantee steady pace if LEVEL › TIME or hand/sensor effects are active. When something “moves by itself,” check the performers before assuming the dial is broken.

For transitions, try a slow CAM MIX move from 25% to 50% to 85%, or ease FEEDBACK down while changing engine, then bring the trails back. Use extreme GLITCH, INVERT or fast SPIN as a deliberate moment rather than the only thing the picture ever does.

chunks.title: Engine versus factory scene
chunks.text:
An **engine** is the kind of visual math. A **factory scene** is an engine plus a styled selection of geometry, motion, color and effects. Engine selection generally leaves your current styling in place. A factory scene resets the relevant visual controls to a baseline and applies its stored values, with many continuous controls easing over roughly a second. It does not reconfigure your audio hardware, camera or recording settings.

| Engine | The feel | Good controls to explore first |
|---|---|---|
| HYPERTUNNEL | A polar tunnel/wormhole with a central rush. | THRUST, SYMMETRY, TWIST, TRAIL ZOOM. |
| KALI VORTEX | Folding fractal structures and dense, jewel-like detail. | DETAIL, MORPH, WARP, FEEDBACK. |
| GYROID CATHEDRAL | A volumetric/raymarched architectural world. | DETAIL, ZOOM, TWIST, THRUST; watch device load. |
| LIQUID PLASMA | Flowing color and melted, cloud-like shapes. | WARP, MORPH, PALETTE, gentle motion. |
| JULIA BLOOM | Fractal islands/blooms with escape-time detail. | DETAIL, MORPH, ZOOM, modest trail spin. |
| CELL DIVISION | Cells with bright edges and organic subdivision. | DENSITY, MORPH, PALETTE, MID › WARP. |
| HYPERSPACE | Star streaks and a sense of forward speed. | THRUST, DENSITY, BLOOM, FEEDBACK. |
| SONIC MANDALA | Layered spectral rings and radial patterns. | SYMMETRY, DETAIL, DENSITY, audio gain. |
| NEON HORIZON | Retro horizon, sun and outrun grid. | SYMMETRY OFF, THRUST, SCANLINES, PALETTE. |

chunks.title: Engine versus factory scene
chunks.text:
The nine factory buttons are **DMT GATE, KALI VORTEX, CATHEDRAL, LIQUID SUN, JULIA BLOOM, CELL DIVISION, HYPERSPACE, MANDALA and OUTRUN**. Keyboard 1–9 loads those factory scenes in that order; it is not simply a bare engine-number shortcut.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: Engine versus factory scene
chunks.text: | SCENE ENGINE | 9 engines; default HYPERTUNNEL | Chooses one of the nine procedural shader engines—the basic kind of world you are looking at. Try this: Changing the engine keeps many of your current styling controls. Loading a factory scene also loads a particular setup, so the two actions can look quite different. |

chunks.title: QUICK commands and pins
chunks.text:
**RANDOMIZE / RND** rolls a new engine and selected visual styling values within built-in ranges. It leaves source/device/camera/recording setup alone. **AUTOPILOT** gradually drifts selected parameters over time. **NEXT SCENE** advances the engine. **FREEZE** holds procedural time, **HIDE UI** clears the operator interface, and **FULLSCREEN** asks the browser to expand the app.

Pin a few things you will actually play: CAM MIX, FEEDBACK, BLOOM, TIME and a color control make a useful starting group. Long-hold again to unpin. Pins are shortcuts to the same controls, not independent copies.

chunks.title: The four memory banks: A–D
chunks.text:
1. Get a look you like.
2. Hold a slot for about half a second to store it. A filled slot is indicated visually. A short tap on an empty slot also stores the current look.
3. Tap a filled slot to recall it; holding a filled slot overwrites it.

Banks store the supported visual look controls: scene engine, form, much of motion, color and FX. They do **not** store a complete production session, a track file, input devices, camera setup, AI settings, recording framing, stems or exported media. FREEZE/REVERSE can be stored; automatic drifting is outside the stored look. Disable unwanted automation separately.

**INIT** returns the supported visual/look controls to their built-in initial values. It is not “erase my recordings,” a full app factory reset, or a reset of all device permissions. There is no general undo stack for randomizing, initializing or overwriting a bank, so store a safe look before exploring.

chunks.title: The four memory banks: A–D
chunks.text: Banks and pins are local to that browser/site. There is no in-app bank-export/import or cloud sync in this version. A saved recording is a finished picture, not a preset you can load back into the dials.

chunks.title: 6. INPUT: choose what the app hears
chunks.text:
The main rig has **one active analysis source at a time**. Switching from a file/demo to MIC or SYSTEM changes what drives the visual; it is not a two-deck DJ crossfader. You can add a separate microphone for recording alongside music from RECORD → AUDIO, but that extra input is a different layer.

| Source | What you get | What to know |
|---|---|---|
| SILENT / SIM | A made-up rhythmic signal so the visuals still move, without a real music track. | Good for experimenting quietly. It can look audio-reactive even though no microphone is being heard. |
| DEMO | The built-in generative “Phase Lock” arrangement, 124 BPM. | Actual sound; convenient for testing a whole recording flow. Scrubbing jumps through the arrangement. |
| FILE | A locally selected audio file, such as MP3, WAV or M4A if the browser can decode it. | The file plays in the app and loops. Use the dock strip to seek. Pick the file again after a fresh session; there is no persistent track library/playlist importer. |
| MIC / BT | A browser-exposed microphone input: built-in mic, headset, USB interface or another OS-provided device. | Pair/connect the hardware in the operating system first. Allow the browser permission, then choose the input under INPUT DEVICE. |
| SYSTEM | Captured tab/desktop audio through the browser's sharing picker, where supported. | Primarily a desktop option. It is hidden on touch-oriented/mobile layouts and when the browser lacks the required API. Choose an audio-sharing option in the picker; sharing a screen without audio provides no usable audio source. |

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text:
Open **INPUT → MIC / BT**, allow access, and check **INPUT DEVICE**. Tap **SCAN** if the list is out of date. Tap the device you actually want; names may remain vague until permission has been granted. Watch the input meter and status readout, not just the existence of a device name.

Bluetooth labels are helpful hints rather than a direct Bluetooth pairing system. A headset in call mode may have thin high frequencies and extra delay. For a tighter music response, a wired interface/USB route is often easier to control. Your phone still decides which interfaces and input routes Chrome can see.

For direct music feeds, start with ECHO CANCEL, NOISE SUPPRESS and AUTO LEVEL off. For speech near speakers, try the processing options one at a time. These are browser/device requests, so their exact behavior can vary.

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text:
| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text: | INPUT TRIM | 0–4×; default 1.00× | Boosts or reduces the live microphone/system input before analysis and the recorder's input tap. This is software gain, so it cannot fix distortion already coming from a clipped hardware input. Try this: Start at 1×. Raise it for a weak input; lower it if the level meter is constantly slammed. It affects the captured live-source signal as well as visual response. |

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text: | NOISE GATE | 0–50%; default 4% | Ignores low-level energy when the rig analyzes live microphone/system audio. It quiets unwanted visual twitching from room noise; it is not a general-purpose noise-removal effect on your saved audio. Try this: Start around 2–6%. Raise it until the room stops triggering the picture, then stop. Too much makes quiet passages look unresponsive. |

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text: | ECHO CANCEL | OFF / ON; default OFF | Asks the microphone/browser to cancel speaker sound getting back into the mic. Try this: Useful for talking near speakers. For a direct music feed, start OFF so processing does not flatten the music; changing it reconnects the main mic input. |

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text: | NOISE SUPPRESS | OFF / ON; default OFF | Asks the microphone/browser to suppress steady background noise. Try this: Try it for voice in a noisy room. Leave it OFF for a clean interface or music feed unless it solves a real problem. Device support varies; changing it reconnects the main mic. |

chunks.title: Get a live mic or interface working
chunks.text: | AUTO LEVEL | OFF / ON; default OFF | Asks the microphone/browser to automatically ride the input level. Try this: Handy for uneven speech. It can soften the difference between quiet sections and big drops, so try OFF for deliberate music dynamics. Changing it reconnects the main mic. |

chunks.title: Three different gain jobs
chunks.text:
- **INPUT TRIM:** changes the live input signal. It can affect both captured live audio and the analysis.
- **REACT → INPUT GAIN:** changes how strongly the analysis drives the visuals. Use this to make a weak-looking response stronger without turning the recorded mix up.
- **RECORD → AUDIO recording gains:** change what goes into the saved mix, independently of visual response. Use these to balance music against voice.

Do not try to solve a visual sensitivity problem by making the saved audio painfully loud. Likewise, lowering recording gain cannot repair audio that is already clipped at the microphone/interface.

The main live microphone is not automatically sent to speakers for monitoring. For intentional monitoring, use the recording audio controls and headphones. Speaker sound can feed back into a mic and can also make the visual react twice to the same musical event.

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text:
These dials describe the engine, so their visual meaning changes a little from world to world. DENSITY in a tunnel is not the exact same thing as DENSITY in cells. Find the range that reads well in the current engine rather than chasing a supposedly perfect number.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | DETAIL | 0–100%; default 55% | Sets geometric/iteration detail in the active visual engine. Try this: More detail can look richer and cost more GPU time, especially in fractal/raymarch scenes. Around 30–60% is a sensible phone starting range. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | ZOOM | 0.3–3×; default 1.00× | Changes the scale or zoom of the active engine's geometry. Try this: Try 0.8×, 1× and 1.3×. Because engines construct their worlds differently, a larger number does not look like the exact same camera move in every scene. This is different from recorded-output Zoom. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | SYMMETRY | OFF through 16-FOLD; default 6-FOLD | Sets kaleidoscope-style symmetry: OFF or 2–16 folds. Try this: OFF is useful for recognizable camera/scan compositions and the horizon scene. 4–8 folds is a nice middle ground; 12–16 can become dense and mandala-like. Individual engines interpret symmetry differently. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | WARP | 0 to 2; default 0.60 | Distorts the underlying procedural space or pattern. Try this: Raise it gradually to make the world bend and melt. If the image stops reading clearly, ease WARP back before piling on other effects. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | DENSITY | 0–100%; default 50% | Changes how tightly packed or frequent the engine's repeated shapes are. Try this: Use it to make the picture busier or more spacious. It affects pattern content rather than recording pixel resolution or the 3D point count. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | MORPH | 0–100%; default 40% | Moves the engine through variations of its internal shape. Try this: Think of it as a character dial: a small move can uncover a very different look. It does not automatically crossfade between different shader engines. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | TWIST | -2 to 2; default 0.30 | Adds directional twist/spiral structure; 0 is neutral and negative/positive values twist differently. Try this: Try −0.3 and +0.3 with moderate symmetry. Small moves can change a tunnel or fractal a lot; it is a shape control rather than the continuous SPIN speed. |

chunks.title: 7. FORM: sculpt the world
chunks.text: | SPECTRUM RING | OFF / ON; default OFF | Draws a live frequency-spectrum ring over the procedural image. Try this: Useful when you want the audio response to be obvious. Turn it off for a cleaner camera-led composition; it follows the main visual/camera crossfade. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text:
TIME advances the engine's clock; THRUST is the amount of travel through its world; SPIN rotates it; ORIGIN places the center. Those jobs overlap visually, but they are different controls. If a scene feels dizzy, lower SPIN and WOBBLE first and keep THRUST moderate.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | TIME | 0–3×; default 1.00× | Sets the procedural animation clock speed. Try this: 1× is the normal pace; 0 stops that clock, but audio modulation and some live/post effects can still move. For a slow backdrop, try 0.3–0.6× before freezing everything. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | ORIGIN | −1 to +1; default center | Moves the visual's horizontal origin using the shared ORIGIN XY pad. Try this: Drag left/right to place the center. This is creative composition inside the rig; output framing has its own left/right control. Double-tap the XY pad to return both axes to center. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | ORIGIN Y | −1 to +1; default center | Moves the visual's vertical origin on the same ORIGIN XY pad. Try this: Drag up/down to place the center. ORIGIN Y is the second axis, not a separate screen that you need to find. Keep it near center when a symmetrical scene should stay balanced. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | SPIN | -1 to 1; default 0.10 | Sets continuous visual rotation speed; negative and positive values turn in opposite directions. Try this: 0 stops this rotation. Around ±0.05–0.2 is usually easier to watch than a full-speed spin. Physical gyro and hand gestures can add their own movement. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | THRUST | 0–3×; default 1.00× | Controls how fast you move through the active engine's world. Try this: Most obvious in tunnels and HYPERSPACE. It works with TIME and may have a subtler interpretation in flat scenes. Raise it for forward rush without using a huge continuous spin. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | WOBBLE | 0–100%; default 20% | Adds a gentle moving wobble to the procedural view. Try this: A little keeps a static look alive. Lower it for geometric precision or if the composition feels seasick. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | FREEZE | OFF / ON; default OFF | Stops the rig's procedural time progression while leaving audio-driven movement possible. Try this: Use it for a held moment on a beat. It is not a still-image capture, does not pause the camera, and is not the recorder's Pause button. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | REVERSE | OFF / ON; default OFF | Runs the procedural clock backward. Try this: It can reverse time-based travel/animation without reversing your music, camera video or recorded file. Combine with a modest TIME value for a readable transition. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | AUTOPILOT | OFF / ON; default OFF | Lets the rig periodically drift selected creative parameters on its own. Try this: Good for an unattended background. Turn it off if you want a dial to stay where you put it; it is separate from the song-aware AI DIRECTOR. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: | DRIFT RATE | 0–100%; default 45% | Controls how frequently AUTOPILOT chooses new drifting targets. Try this: Low is more leisurely, high changes direction more often. It has no effect when AUTOPILOT is off and is not the same as AI CHANGE RATE. |

chunks.title: 8. MOTION: set the pace and point of view
chunks.text: **Freeze is not record-pause.** FREEZE can leave camera motion, audio-reactive geometry, feedback/post effects and live gestures active. Recorder Pause actually leaves that time out of the take. Music Play/Pause is a third, separate action.

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text:
Start with PALETTE and HUE. Then set EXPOSURE and CONTRAST so shapes remain readable. Add SATURATION last. If you are mixing a face into the image, judge skin and background together—bright neon, strong contrast and colored trails can take over quickly.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | PALETTE | 6 palettes; default SPECTRA | Chooses SPECTRA, ACID, SOLAR, GLACIER, CANDY, or TOXIN. Try this: Find a palette you like before fine-tuning HUE. The same palette can look very different at different exposure, saturation and blend settings. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | HUE | 0–360°; default 0° | Offsets the procedural palette's color position. Try this: Use it to find a color family that suits your track or branding. It interacts with HUE DRIFT and any compass/hand modulation, so turn those down if you want a fixed hue. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | HUE DRIFT | 0–100%; default 15% | Continuously drifts the palette hue. Try this: 0% keeps the automatic hue clock still; a little drift is good for long ambient passages. It does not stop an AI or sensor from changing the overall look. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | EXPOSURE | 0–2×; default 1.05× | Scales the final picture's brightness/exposure. Try this: Start near 1×. If the image looks like a white blob, lower this and BLOOM first. This control grades the visual synthesizer track. Use Camera FX → Exposure for the camera itself. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | SATURATION | 0–200%; default 115% | Sets how much color survives in the final visual grade. Try this: 0% is grayscale, 100% is normal color amount, and higher values push it harder. More is not always richer—very high values can flatten color detail. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | CONTRAST | 0.5–2×; default 1.10× | Separates dark and bright parts of the image. Try this: Around 1× is a useful neutral point. Higher contrast can make the picture punchier but crush detail; lower contrast is softer. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | TRAIL HUE | -0.1 to 0.1; default +0.006 | Shifts the color of feedback history as it repeats; negative and positive values move the shift in opposite directions. Try this: It needs visible FEEDBACK to matter. Tiny values go a long way because the change repeats frame after frame. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | POSTERIZE | 0–100%; default 0% | Reduces smooth shading to fewer visible color bands. Try this: Keep 0% for smooth gradients. Raise it for a graphic, print-like or retro look; strong settings can make faces look harsh in a blend. |

chunks.title: 9. COLOR: choose the mood, then protect the detail
chunks.text: | INVERT | OFF / ON; default OFF | Turns the final image into a negative-style image. Try this: Use it as a momentary change of mood. BEAT INVERT is a separate rhythmic toggle; combining them changes which part of the cycle looks negative. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text:
FEEDBACK, TRAIL ZOOM, TRAIL SPIN, TRAIL WARP and TRAIL HUE work on history. BLOOM, CHROMA, GLITCH, LENS and texture controls change the current final look. If a trail-related control seems to do nothing, make sure enough FEEDBACK exists to reveal it.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | FEEDBACK | 0–99%; default 84% | How much of the previous picture remains in the next one—the main trail length control. Try this: Around 50–75% is easier to keep readable; 85–95% gives longer, more immersive history. Near the top it can smear or accumulate brightness. Drop it to 0 to let old trails clear. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | TRAIL ZOOM | -0.05 to 0.05; default +0.012 | Makes feedback history expand inward/outward relative to the center. Try this: Positive values produce a zooming-in/expanding-history feel; negative values pull history the other way. Try about ±0.005–0.015. 0 stops this particular trail motion. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | TRAIL SPIN | -0.05 to 0.05; default +0.004 | Rotates the previous image a little on every feedback pass. Try this: Tiny positive/negative values make spirals in opposite directions. Pair it with FEEDBACK around 70–85%; large values can turn the whole view into a spinning smear. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | TRAIL WARP | 0–100%; default 20% | Warps the old trail image before mixing it back in. Try this: This makes history look liquid without being the same dial as FORM WARP. Keep it low when you want clean geometric echoes. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | CHROMA | 0–100%; default 30% | Separates red, green and blue sampling slightly for color fringes. Try this: Around 10–25% can add energy. Reduce it for readable faces, small text or clean edges. HIGH › CHROMA can add more on top of your base setting. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | BLOOM | 0–150%; default 75% | Adds a glowing halo around bright parts. Try this: A little glow goes a long way when FEEDBACK is high. Values can go above 100%, so check that you are not turning every highlight into a white patch. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | GLITCH | 0–100%; default 8% | Adds digital blocks, horizontal shifts and broken-image accents. Try this: Keep it near zero for a clean visual, and bring it up briefly for transitions. The DIRECTOR's drop effects can add extra glitch even if this base dial is low. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | LENS | -1 to 1; default 0.15 | Bends the final image with a lens-like warp; negative and positive values bend differently. Try this: 0 is neutral. Try a little for a curved tunnel or wide-lens feeling; stronger settings can distort a camera/visual blend. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | MIRROR | OFF, X, XY, QUAD, 5–16-SPLIT; default OFF | Chooses OFF, X, XY, QUAD, or any radial split count from 5 through 16 for the final visual. Try this: X folds horizontally; XY folds both directions; QUAD adds a more complex fold. The 5–16-SPLIT choices repeat and reflect the picture around the center, like a kaleidoscope. This is an artistic effect, separate from normal front-camera mirroring. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | SWIRL | −1 to +1; default 0 | Twists the whole picture around the center, strongest near the middle. Negative and positive turn the twist in opposite directions. Try this: Start at ±0.15–0.3 with a 6-SPLIT or 8-SPLIT mirror. 0 is neutral. This Visual FX control reshapes the synthesizer only. Use CAMERA → CAMERA FX → Swirl for camera-only treatment. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | RIPPLE | 0–100%; default 0% | Adds moving circular waves to the entire picture, like ripples spreading through a lens. Try this: Start at 10–25% with modest feedback. Silence Stop holds its animation when the selected input becomes quiet. It is separate from SENSE → TOUCH MODE → RIPPLE. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | WAVE | 0–100%; default 0% | Makes the picture undulate horizontally and vertically with animated sine waves. Try this: Start at 10–20% for a watery bend, then try a radial mirror. Combine gently with SWIRL; high values of every warp at once can hide the original subject. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | PIXELATE | 0–100%; default 0% | Turns the picture into larger pixel blocks. Try this: Low settings give a retro texture; high settings hide detail fast. It is a look, not a smaller export file or a recording-resolution setting. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | SCANLINES | 0–100%; default 22% | Adds horizontal display/CRT-style scanlines. Try this: Try 10–30% for a light screen texture. It does not change actual frame rate or interlace the video. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | GRAIN | 0–100%; default 18% | Adds a moving noise texture. Try this: A little makes a clean digital scene feel less clinical. High grain can look messy and make compressed uploads harder to keep clean. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text: | VIGNETTE | 0–150%; default 80% | Darkens the edges so the center feels more prominent. Try this: Start low when important content sits near the corners. High values make a strong tunnel/spotlight feel and can hide edge details. |

chunks.title: 10. FX: trails, glow, lens and texture
chunks.text:
**Try a new kaleidoscope mix:** Choose MIRROR → 6-SPLIT or 8-SPLIT, set SWIRL around 0.2, RIPPLE around 15%, and keep WAVE at 0 until the first two feel right. Then introduce WAVE slowly. Every radial split from 5 through 16 is available; higher counts produce finer repeated wedges. These controls now belong to the independent visual synthesizer track. To repeat or warp only the camera, use CAMERA → CAMERA FX. The dedicated camera kaleidoscope has every division from 1 through 16.

**A clean reset for an overloaded look:** lower FEEDBACK to 0 for a moment, set GLITCH and POSTERIZE to 0, set EXPOSURE near 1×, reduce BLOOM, and switch off rhythmic inversion/strobe. Bring only the useful bits back. 100% CAM MIX keeps Camera FX. To see the untreated camera, bypass Camera FX; this does not reset the visual synthesizer.

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text:
The visual analyzer groups sound into bass, mids and highs. You choose which visual behavior each group pushes. Start with a good input level, then set a response you can feel at a comfortable scale. A short test with a clear beat is easier to tune than a noisy room full of competing sounds.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | INPUT GAIN | 0–3×; default 1.20× | Amplifies the signal used to drive visuals, not the recording's output mix. Try this: Start at 1–1.2×, then raise only if the meters and response are weak. High values can pin the analysis and make everything react all the time; they do not repair a poor audio source. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | BASS › ZOOM | 0–100%; default 35% | Makes bass energy add zoom/scale movement. Try this: Start around 15–35% for a pulse you can read. If every kick makes the whole scene lurch, lower this before reducing the music recording level. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | MID › WARP | 0–100%; default 40% | Lets midrange energy add procedural warp. Try this: It can respond nicely to vocals, guitars and synths. Lower it when dense music makes the visual busy even between kick drums. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | HIGH › CHROMA | 0–100%; default 50% | Makes high-frequency energy add color separation/chroma. Try this: Good for hi-hats and bright percussion. Reduce it if outlines constantly split apart; increase modestly if a thin Bluetooth/call-mode input has weak high-frequency response. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | LEVEL › TIME | 0–100%; default 40% | Makes overall signal level speed up procedural time. Try this: Low values keep the pace more predictable. High values can make loud sections rush forward even when the base TIME dial stays still. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | BEAT THRESHOLD | 1.05–2×; default 1.35× | How strong a bass peak must be relative to recent bass energy to count as a beat. Try this: Lower means easier/more frequent triggers; higher means pickier/fewer triggers. It is not a BPM selector. Adjust after your input level is sensible. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | SMOOTHING | 0–95%; default 60% | How gently analyzed audio values settle instead of dropping abruptly. Try this: Higher gives a smoother, more floaty release; lower feels snappier. If the visual never seems to let go of the last hit, bring this down a bit. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | BEAT PUNCH | OFF / ON; default ON | Adds a short zoom punch on detected beats. Try this: A good first rhythmic effect. If a delicate camera blend is bouncing too much, switch it off before changing the camera framing. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | BEAT STROBE | OFF / ON; default OFF | Adds a white flash on detected beats. Try this: Use deliberately: it produces repeated flashes. Leave it off for viewers sensitive to flashing, and check DROP FX too if you want a flash-free performance. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | BEAT INVERT | OFF / ON; default OFF | Toggles negative/normal-style inversion as beats arrive. Try this: This is a strong rhythmic effect and can also create intense light changes. For a stable grade, leave it off and use the regular COLOR INVERT switch only when wanted. |

chunks.title: 11. REACT: make it dance with the right part of the music
chunks.text: | BEAT JUMP | OFF / ON; default OFF | Chooses a different shader engine every 16 detected beats. Try this: Useful for hands-free variety, but those beats depend on detection. It is not a precisely authored arrangement or a guaranteed musical-bar counter. |

chunks.title: Tune a beat response in four moves
chunks.text:
1. Use a source you can actually hear or meter. SIM will produce a fake pulse, so it cannot prove your microphone is working.
2. Set INPUT GAIN near 1–1.2×. Get B / M / H moving without being permanently pinned high.
3. Bring BASS › ZOOM up slowly. Add MID › WARP and HIGH › CHROMA only if you want those parts of the song to contribute.
4. Set BEAT THRESHOLD for sensible hits, then adjust SMOOTHING for a crisp or floaty release. Check several quiet and loud passages.

A house groove and a drumless ambient track will not detect the same way. The BPM readout and BEAT JUMP use detected events; they are not a sample-accurate synchronization system or external MIDI clock. There is no manual BPM-entry dial in this version.

chunks.title: 12. CAMERA: mix the real world into the visual
chunks.text: Open **CAMERA**, switch the camera on, allow permission, then confirm that the small CAMERA FEED preview is live. Pick FRONT for a selfie or REAR for the room/subject. If the preview is not live, the CAM MIX dial has no camera picture to bring in.

chunks.title: The 0–50–100 crossfade
chunks.text:
| CAM MIX position | What you should see in the actual picture |
|---|---|
| 0% | The procedural visual. The little camera preview inside the operator menu can still be live. |
| 1–49% | The selected artistic blend gradually comes in. |
| 50% | The full selected blend of camera and visual. This is not necessarily a mathematical 50/50 opacity blend: SCREEN, ADD and the key modes combine images differently. |
| 51–99% | The complete visual/effect composition fades away toward the camera. |
| 100% | Processed camera-only picture with its dedicated Camera FX and usual crop/front-camera mirroring. Visual-synth effects and history fade out. Bypass Camera FX for the untreated feed. |

chunks.title: The 0–50–100 crossfade
chunks.text: The camera-only endpoint does not hide your operating menus on the screen. For an uncluttered **saved** picture, choose **RECORD → OUTPUT → Menu visibility → Clean** and switch off any optional recorded title, branding, lyrics or skeletons you do not want. Those separately selected output overlays can still be drawn over a camera-only base.

chunks.title: The 0–50–100 crossfade
chunks.text: *These are screenshots of the app using Chrome's synthetic test-camera feed. The green pattern is the test source, not a camera fault or a special Neuroflux effect. Operator controls remain visible; the output profile determines recorded overlays.*

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text:
| BLEND | In ordinary language | A useful starting situation |
|---|---|---|
| SCREEN | A bright, light-over-light combination. Dark parts of the camera contribute less. | Neon patterns over a darker room or a person against a dark background. |
| ADD | Adds camera and visual brightness aggressively. | Short, energetic peaks; lower EXPOSURE/BLOOM if highlights blow out. |
| DIFF | Shows differences between the two pictures, often making unusual contrast/colors. | Abstract performance and silhouettes; less suitable when natural skin color matters. |
| MULTIPLY | Multiplies the two pictures with the app's brightness scaling; darker areas can dominate. | Using camera shapes as texture in the graphic. It is not a precise photographic opacity blend. |
| LUMA KEY | Lets camera brightness decide where the camera replaces the visual. | A bright subject/light against darker surroundings; adjust KEY LEVEL. |
| DEPTH KEY | Uses estimated depth, when available, to decide where to show the camera. | A subject separated in depth from the background. Enable AI DEPTH in 3D for actual depth-based input; without it the shader uses a brightness fallback. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text:
These are blend/key treatments, not a chroma-key green-screen editor or a guaranteed person-cutout tool. Depth edges can shimmer and a brightness key can also pick out bright objects in the background.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | CAMERA | OFF / ON; default OFF | Makes the live camera available as a visible layer in the main picture. Try this: Switch it on and allow access. If hands/depth still need the camera, hiding the camera layer may leave the hardware active for those features. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | FACING | FRONT, REAR; default REAR | Chooses FRONT or REAR camera, subject to the cameras the browser actually exposes. Try this: REAR is the default. FRONT is useful for selfies and hand conducting and is mirrored in the visual mix. Switching can briefly reopen the camera. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | CAM MIX | 0–100%; default 70% | The main camera/visual crossfader: 0% is visuals, 50% is the full selected blend, and 100% is camera only. Above 50%, the complete visual/effect picture fades toward the camera. Try this: Use 25–40% to introduce the camera, 50% for the strongest selected blend, and 70–90% to bring the person or room forward. At 100%, Camera FX stay visible while visual-synth trails and grading fade away; operator menus can still be visible on your screen. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | BLEND | SCREEN, ADD, DIFF, MULTIPLY, LUMA KEY, DEPTH KEY; default SCREEN | Selects SCREEN, ADD, DIFF, MULTIPLY, LUMA KEY, or DEPTH KEY. It changes the mixed look, not the 0%/100% endpoints. Try this: SCREEN is a friendly first choice. Compare the modes at 50% CAM MIX so you are actually seeing the full blend character. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | KEY LEVEL | 0–100%; default 50% | Moves the threshold for LUMA KEY or DEPTH KEY. Try this: In LUMA KEY, higher values generally restrict replacement to brighter camera areas. In DEPTH KEY, adjust while watching the preview; it is a depth threshold, not an exact distance in meters. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | EDGE GLOW | 0–100%; default 35% | Finds edges in the camera and adds colored glow to them. Try this: Around 10–25% can outline a person without overwhelming the image. It scales in with the first half of CAM MIX and disappears again at the camera-only endpoint. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | CAM WARP | 0–100%; default 0% | A shortcut to the camera-only Local lens effect. Raising it adds/enables that effect in the camera stack; zero bypasses it. It uses one stack slot and stays visible at 100% CAM MIX. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | MOTION › PULSE | 0–100%; default 50% | Uses changes between camera frames to trigger visual pulse/beat energy. Try this: Move a hand or walk across the shot to test it. Camera shake can also trigger it; lower the amount for handheld filming if the picture punches constantly. |

chunks.title: Choose a blend at 50%, then choose your final balance
chunks.text: | CAM TRAILS | OFF / ON; default OFF | Adds/enables Camera trails in the camera-only stack. Turning it off bypasses that node. It uses one stack slot; the visual synthesizer keeps its own separate feedback history. |

chunks.title: A practical face-and-visual mix
chunks.text:
Use SCREEN, start at 30% CAM MIX, keep EDGE GLOW around 10–20%, and keep CAM WARP low. Move to 50% to see the full artistic blend. If the face is lost in the effects, move toward 75–90% instead of only pushing exposure. Move all the way to 100% for a clean camera reveal; crossfade back to bring the visual world in again.

**If 100% still looks like the old blended endpoint:** finish active work, open the [update recovery page](https://neuroflux-rig.vercel.app/update.html), and tap UPDATE AND OPEN NEUROFLUX on that phone/browser. A regular refresh can leave an old offline version active. Browser profiles and different phones keep their own caches.

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text:
Start in a comfortable position, enable MOTION SENSORS, answer any permission prompt, and tap **RE-ZERO**. Re-zero takes the current orientation as your reference; use it again after you change how you hold the phone. It does not calibrate the microphone or repair missing hardware support.

The SENSOR ARRAY/status area distinguishes readings the browser exposes from estimated/unavailable ones. Tilt and gyro need motion/orientation access. Heading needs usable compass/orientation data. Light can be camera-estimated when a real light sensor is not available. A desktop cannot respond like a handheld phone just because the switch is on.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | MOTION SENSORS | OFF / ON; default OFF | Turns on the motion/orientation sensor listeners and requests permission where required. Try this: Hold your phone in the position you plan to perform from, enable it, then use RE-ZERO. A desktop or a browser that does not expose a sensor may show unavailable readings. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | TILT › ORIGIN | 0–100%; default 50% | Moves the center of the visual as you tilt the device. Try this: Around 15–35% gives a gentle handheld feel. Higher values are more like steering the scene around the screen. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | TILT › FLOW | 0–100%; default 50% | Uses tilt to push the trail/feedback flow. Try this: It is easiest to see with FEEDBACK turned up. Keep it low for a stable image; turn it up for drifting, liquid trails. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | GYRO › SPIN | 0–100%; default 40% | Uses rotational motion from the device to add spin. Try this: Small wrist turns can add a lot of life. Lower it if the image keeps turning when you want a steady composition. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | SHAKE › PUNCH | 0–100%; default 60% | Turns a physical shake into a visual punch or burst of energy. Try this: Use a small, deliberate gesture first. It depends on motion data, so a browser without accelerometer access cannot supply this trigger. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | TOUCH FX | OFF / ON; default ON | Lets fingers or a mouse bend the visual canvas where you touch it. Try this: Leave ON for performance effects. With it ON, use two fingers to swipe between scenes; a single finger is your effect controller. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | TOUCH MODE | RIPPLE, VORTEX, LENS, SHOCK; default RIPPLE | Chooses RIPPLE, VORTEX, LENS, or SHOCK for the touch field. Try this: RIPPLE sends out rings; VORTEX swirls; LENS bends/magnifies; SHOCK gives a more abrupt energetic disturbance. Try each with TOUCH FORCE around 40%. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | TOUCH FORCE | 0–100%; default 70% | Sets the strength of canvas touches and touch-style hand pinches. Try this: Reduce it for subtle accents or small screens. Higher values are good for a few obvious performance gestures rather than constant dragging. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | COMPASS › HUE | 0–100%; default 50% | Adds a color offset from the device's heading/compass information. Try this: Turn slowly to feel the palette respond. If there is no usable heading data, this control cannot invent one. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: | LIGHT › GLOW | 0–100%; default 50% | Lets ambient light influence glow. The app can use a light sensor when exposed, or estimate scene brightness from the active camera. Try this: Darker surroundings can produce more glow. Set this to 0% if you want BLOOM to stay consistent while lighting changes. |

chunks.title: 13. SENSE: perform with your phone and fingers
chunks.text: For your first sensor mix, try TILT › ORIGIN 20%, TILT › FLOW 15% and GYRO › SPIN 10–20%, leaving a readable base scene. Hold the phone still and re-zero if the view drifts. For a locked-off recording, turn motion sensors off and leave touch gestures for intentional accents.

chunks.title: 14. 3D: depth clouds and imported scans
chunks.text: There are two separate jobs on this page: **AI DEPTH** estimates a point cloud from the live camera; **LOAD SPLAT** opens an existing scan file. Neither is a full in-app room-scanning/capture workflow.

chunks.title: Live camera depth
chunks.text:
Switch on AI DEPTH and wait for the first download/initialization to finish. The app tries supported GPU acceleration and can fall back to a local CPU/WASM path. The model runs on the device; first-time model/runtime downloads need internet. A depth model can be a substantial download, so use the status message rather than guessing that a short delay means failure.

Begin with DEPTH RES FAST and CLOUD DENSITY LOW or MEDIUM. Bring CLOUD GAIN and POINT SIZE up until the cloud is readable. Then try a little ORBIT and BASS › BURST. A brightly lit, distinct subject is easier to read than a dim, blank wall. The estimated depth is relative and imperfect, not survey-grade distance data.

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text:
1. Export a supported **.ply**, **.splat** or **.spz** file from your scanning workflow.
2. Tap **LOAD SPLAT**, choose the file, and wait for the “loaded” status.
3. Start with SPLAT GAIN around 50–60% and SPLAT DENSITY low enough to run smoothly.
4. Toggle SPLAT FLIP if the orientation is wrong; reduce SPLAT SPIN to 0 while you inspect it.
5. Add ORBIT, spin or bass burst gradually. Use **CLEAR** to unload the imported scan from the current rig.

A file extension alone is not a promise: unsupported PLY layouts/SPZ variants or damaged files can fail to parse. The renderer centers/scales imported point data and can reduce a very dense source to fit its working point budget (up to roughly 600,000 imported points before density reduction). This is a lightweight point/splat performance view, not a full-quality Gaussian-splat editing or reconstruction application. Clearing does not delete the original file on your device.

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text:
| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | AI DEPTH | OFF / ON; default OFF | Uses a downloaded AI model to estimate depth from the camera and make a live colored point cloud. Try this: Give it time to load the first time. This is estimated single-camera depth, not a LiDAR measurement or an automatic saved 3D scan. It can turn the camera on if necessary. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | DEPTH RES | FAST, BALANCED, FINE; default FAST | Chooses FAST, BALANCED, or FINE for the depth-estimation input. Try this: Start FAST on a phone. Move up only if the cloud stays responsive and the device is comfortable. FINE means more work for the model, not guaranteed perfect edges. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | CLOUD DENSITY | LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH; default MEDIUM | Chooses LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH point density for the live depth cloud. Try this: This is separate from DEPTH RES: one controls the model input, the other how many points draw the result. Lower density first if the cloud is sluggish. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | CLOUD GAIN | 0–150%; default 50% | Sets how strongly the live depth cloud is drawn. Try this: Use a little cloud over the visual for texture, or raise it to make the cloud the main attraction. 0% hides the cloud without being the same thing as turning the whole depth engine off. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | POINT SIZE | 0.3–3×; default 1.00× | Changes the size of live-cloud points. Try this: Small points look more delicate; larger points fill gaps and look chunkier. The effect is easiest to judge together with CLOUD DENSITY. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | BASS › BURST | 0–100%; default 50% | Lets bass and spectral energy spread the 3D points outward. Try this: Keep low to preserve a person's shape or an imported object. Raise it for the exploding-on-the-beat effect; it applies to the 3D rendering rather than changing your original scan file. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | ORBIT | 0–100%; default 60% | Sets how much the 3D view orbits, including tilt-based and gentle automatic movement. Try this: Use a little for depth and parallax. Reduce it when the object keeps drifting away from a composition you like; motion sensors provide the physical tilt part when available. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | SPLAT GAIN | 0–150%; default 60% | Controls the visible strength of an imported splat/point scan. Try this: Start near 40–60%. If nothing changes, check that a file is loaded; this dial does not create a scan by itself. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | SPLAT DENSITY | 5–100%; default 60% | Chooses what fraction of the loaded scan points are drawn. Try this: Lower it for speed or a more airy point-cloud look. Higher values make the scan fuller and cost more GPU time. It does not increase the detail in the source file. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | SPLAT SPIN | -1 to 1; default 0.15 | Sets continuous spin for the imported scan; negative and positive values turn in opposite directions. Try this: 0 stops the automatic spin. Try a small magnitude such as 0.05–0.15 before using a full turntable effect. |

chunks.title: Load a scan you already have
chunks.text: | SPLAT FLIP | OFF / ON; default ON | Flips the imported scan's Y/Z orientation to help correct an upside-down load. Try this: Toggle it if a scan looks inverted. The loader already chooses a starting value by format; there is no universal flip setting for every scanning app. |

chunks.title: 15. AI: prompts, director, hands and lyrics
chunks.text: This tab contains several independent features. Local audio analysis/director behavior and local camera models are different from requests sent to Gemini. You can make a great recording without using any online AI.

chunks.title: Get a fresh, guided walkthrough
chunks.text:
Open **Menu → AI → GUIDED WALKTHROUGH**. **WALKTHROUGH MODE starts OFF.** Turn its switch ON only when you want help; the app remembers that choice. Even with it enabled, a new session waits for you to begin or resume a walkthrough. Tell it what you want to do in ordinary language: “Help me record a clean portrait camera mix with music and a separate voice track,” or “Show me how to make a six-split kaleidoscope with a gentle swirl.” You can also choose **GUIDE ME STEP BY STEP** in the typed AI command window.

The guide looks up relevant parts of this manual and checks your current settings and browser capabilities. It makes a new plan for that setup. Read the plan first, then press **BEGIN WALKTHROUGH**. Building the plan does not change a setting or start a take.

chunks.title: Get a fresh, guided walkthrough
chunks.text:
The current step sits inside the app's native menu. On phones, the menu expands so the instructions and controls have room. A green outline points to the real control. Use **SHOW CONTROL** to find it again. Turn the dial yourself or tap **APPLY THIS SETTING**. **VERIFIED · NEXT** means the app has checked that setting. It does not mean the result sounds or looks good—that part is yours. Listening and visual checks say **I CHECKED THIS · NEXT**, because the guide cannot judge them for you.

Use **UNDO CHANGE** for a reversible setting, **SKIP** when a step is unnecessary, the minus button to minimize, or × to turn walkthrough mode OFF. You can also switch it OFF in the AI panel. Turning it off dismisses the highlighting and instructions, cancels a pending guide request and clears the resumable plan. Your visual/audio settings and any recording already in progress stay as you left them. **Change the plan / I'm stuck** lets you describe a problem and rebuild the remaining steps using the latest settings. If you reload the same tab, an explicit **RESUME WALKTHROUGH** lets you continue.

chunks.title: Get a fresh, guided walkthrough
chunks.text:
Starting a recording still needs your own tap on **START TAKE · 3–2–1**, followed by the normal countdown. Camera and microphone permissions still come from the browser. Read the step before granting access. The guide does not silently record, delete takes, upload files or publish anything. Its instructions and highlighting stay out of your recorded picture.

Each step has **Manual sources** so you can read the explanation. The plan names the model that answered. It tries **Gemini 3.8 Flash first**; if that is unavailable, a working Flash fallback is clearly labeled. This does not mean 3.8 handled a request that actually used another model.

Online guidance sends your written goal, numeric controls, supported recording/audio settings and browser capability flags to the app's Gemini service. It does not send source files, filenames, camera frames, recorded audio, lyric text, titles, branding text or API keys. Ordinary controls and recordings keep working if online guidance is unavailable. If the guide reports an older catalog, finish your take and use **SYSTEM → APP UPDATES → LOAD LATEST VERSION**.

chunks.title: Type or speak a visual idea
chunks.text:
Tap the dock's sparkle button or **TYPE A VIBE**, write a clear request, and submit it. Start with concrete creative changes:

- “Slow blue tunnel, soft glow, almost no glitch.”
- “Keep the current scene, lower the feedback and make the bass response gentle.”
- “A warm liquid plasma look with no strobe.”
- “Switch to the horizon scene, reduce spin and make the colors colder.”

The service translates the request into supported visual parameters/commands. It is not generating a new filmed video or writing an arbitrary shader from scratch. Check the result with your own eyes; broad instructions can be interpreted in several ways.

Hold the dock AI button to speak, or use **HOLD TO TALK**. Release after a short instruction. The voice capture is short (up to about nine seconds), and very short/silent clips may be rejected. The app may duck music monitoring while you speak. If the browser cannot open the mic, use typing instead.

chunks.title: Type or speak a visual idea
chunks.text: **CHECK** refreshes the Gemini connection status. If the app reports no server key or an unavailable service, ordinary visuals/recording still work. The owner connects Gemini on the server; a guest should not paste an API key into a public prompt or share it in a recording. Usage/availability depends on the connected provider and its limits.

chunks.title: AI DIRECTOR versus AUTOPILOT
chunks.text:
AUTOPILOT drifts selected parameters. The DIRECTOR follows changes in the analyzed song energy and classifies broad sections such as **INTRO, GROOVE, BUILD, DROP, DRIVE and BREAK**. The song map and energy history show what it thinks is happening. It is a live estimate, not an imported cue sheet or a guaranteed prediction of an upcoming drop.

With GEMINI LOOKS off or unavailable, a local plan still supplies groove/build/drop/break looks. With Gemini connected and that switch on, the service can design the plan. DRIVE sets how hard modulation pushes; CHANGE RATE influences how often it looks for groove/drive changes. Manual edits get a short grace period before automatic look changes resume, but modulation can still be audible/visible in the result. Turn the director off if a value must stay fixed.

chunks.title: AI DIRECTOR versus AUTOPILOT
chunks.text: **LIKE** stores feedback about a look you enjoy. **SKIP** marks the current look as unwanted and chooses another. That taste is stored in this browser, not a universal model retrained for every user. **REPLAN** asks for/rebuilds the section plan. Local planning remains available when an online look request cannot complete.

chunks.title: Conduct with your hands
chunks.text:
Enable HAND TRACKING, let the model load, and make sure your hands appear in the preview. It opens the front camera if it needs to open its own camera, but an already-active rear camera can remain in use—choose **CAMERA → FACING → FRONT** deliberately for self-conducting.

| Gesture | Effect |
|---|---|
| Raise/lower your hands | Adds or reduces energy-related speed/brightness/glow modulation. |
| Move left/right | Shifts color/hue. |
| Open/close your hands | Changes warp strength. |
| Use two hands, move apart/together | Changes zoom/scale. |
| Tilt the line between two hands | Adds visual twist/rotation. |
| Pinch thumb and index finger | Acts like a touch effect at the tracked fingertip when PINCH FX is enabled. |
| Fist, then open quickly | Triggers a burst/punch, which can include a flash. |
| Fast open-hand swipe | Can change to the next/previous scene. |

chunks.title: Conduct with your hands
chunks.text: Use good lighting, keep hands in frame, and begin with HAND FORCE around 30–50%. SHOW SKELETON affects the operator overlay; the saved video's Hand skeletons option is separate. Hiding the visible camera layer does not necessarily release a camera still needed by hands/depth. Turning tracking off is how to stop tracking.

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text:
Enable LIVE LYRICS with real music/vocals or a live input. **PREVIEW** inserts sample words so you can try typography without treating that as successful transcription. LANGUAGE guides recognition; it does not translate a song into another language. IMPACT, FLOW and KARAOKE change the live presentation.

STREAM uses an online live-transcription connection; CLIP sends short audio chunks and is normally a few seconds behind. A failed stream can fall back to CLIP. Noise, overlapping voices and music can cause missing/misheard words. The current output recorder renders selected recognized text as a simpler overlay; it does not copy the exact on-screen kinetic typography or promise subtitle-file export.

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text:
Recording silence does not automatically stop online lyric analysis. If you do not want lyric audio transmitted, turn LIVE LYRICS off, rather than only muting the recorded mix.

| Control | Range / initial default | What it does, and how to mix it |
|---|---|---|

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | AI DIRECTOR | OFF / ON; default OFF | Listens to the main analysis and performs looks according to detected song energy/sections. Try this: Give it a few seconds to listen. It can use a local plan without a Gemini key; online Gemini-designed looks are an optional additional layer. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | DRIVE | 0–100%; default 65% | Sets the DIRECTOR's modulation strength: how hard builds, drops and energy changes push the visual. Try this: Try 25–45% when you still want to steer manually. Higher feels more dramatic. It is a creative intensity control, not the audio recording volume. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | CHANGE RATE | 0–100%; default 50% | Sets how frequently the DIRECTOR looks for beat-aligned changes in groove/drive sections. Try this: Lower gives longer-held looks; higher checks more often. Changes remain conditional, so a higher value does not guarantee a new scene at a fixed interval. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | GEMINI LOOKS | OFF / ON; default ON | Lets the connected Gemini service design a plan of looks for song sections. Try this: If Gemini is unavailable, the local director can still make a plan. Turn this off to keep planning local; text prompts/voice/lyrics have their own online requirements. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | DROP FX | OFF / ON; default ON | Allows the DIRECTOR's drop flashes, shocks and glitch hits. Try this: Turn off for a gentler set or when you want to avoid drop flashes. Also disable BEAT STROBE/BEAT INVERT and avoid burst gestures if flashes are unwanted. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | HAND TRACKING | OFF / ON; default OFF | Tracks up to two hands with the active camera, loading the hand model on first use. Try this: FRONT camera is easier for conducting. It can use a camera already running on REAR; set FACING deliberately. Tracking is processed locally after model loading. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | HAND FORCE | 0–100%; default 70% | How strongly tracked hand movement pushes the scene. Try this: Around 30–50% is easier to learn than full strength. Lower it if small hand movements keep overpowering the look. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | SHOW SKELETON | OFF / ON; default ON | Draws tracked hand skeletons on the operator display. Try this: Turning the drawing off does not turn tracking off. Recorded hand skeletons have a separate option under RECORD → OUTPUT. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | PINCH FX | OFF / ON; default ON | Makes a thumb/index-finger pinch act like a touch at the fingertip. Try this: Choose a TOUCH MODE in SENSE for its character. Keep the hand in frame with clear lighting; pinch recognition is less reliable with occlusion or fast motion. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | LIVE LYRICS | OFF / ON; default OFF | Listens for vocals and turns recognized words into animated on-screen text. Try this: Needs a working Gemini connection and an audible/input signal. Recognition is approximate and can lag or mishear lyrics; preview a take before treating the words as final captions. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | TYPE STYLE | IMPACT, FLOW, KARAOKE; default IMPACT | Chooses IMPACT, FLOW, or KARAOKE for live words. Try this: IMPACT emphasizes individual words; FLOW builds lines; KARAOKE highlights words in a line-style presentation. Recorded lyrics use a simpler text rendering rather than an exact copy of these DOM animations. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | TYPE SIZE | 0.5–1.6×; default 1.00× | Scales the live operator-display lyrics. Try this: Around 1× is the reference size. This does not promise the same size/style in the recording overlay; use the output preview to judge recorded text. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | LANGUAGE | AUTO, ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, FRENCH; default AUTO | Chooses AUTO, ENGLISH, SPANISH, PORTUGUESE, or FRENCH for transcription guidance. Try this: Pick the language you expect if AUTO struggles. It guides recognition; it is not a translation-language selector. |

chunks.title: Live lyrics
chunks.text: | ENGINE | STREAM, CLIP; default STREAM | Chooses STREAM or CLIP transcription. Try this: STREAM means live transcription, not broadcasting your visual to a platform. CLIP listens in roughly four-second chunks with a few seconds of lag; STREAM can fall back to CLIP if live connection fails. |

chunks.title: 16. RECORD: start, pause and save a take
chunks.text: Open **Menu → RECORD**. Its four subtabs are **RECORD, OUTPUT, AUDIO and LIBRARY**. The dock REC shortcut uses your last settings; the menu is where you make intentional changes before the next take.

chunks.title: The whole recording flow
chunks.text:
1. Set the source, visual, camera and effects you want to perform with.
2. In OUTPUT, choose A's shape/resolution/fps, recorded overlays and audio source. If needed, configure B too and enable dual recording in RECORD.
3. In AUDIO, set music/mic recording balance, select/enable an extra mic if needed, and check the meters.
4. In RECORD, choose video or audio-only, optional companion files and an optional duration limit.
5. Use **TEST OUTPUT** for a video configuration. The app renders the selected output(s) for about two seconds and asks for at least 80% of the selected frame rate. A failing test does not secretly drop your resolution; lower the load and test again.
6. Tap **REC** in the dock or **● RECORD · 3–2–1** in the page. Preparation can take a moment. Every new take then shows 3, 2, 1 for about a second each. Nothing is captured during those three seconds.
7. During that countdown, **CANCEL**, Escape, or the dock preparation control cancels the take and removes its empty prepared files.
8. When capture begins, the recording menu closes. Change the visuals as usual. The dock shows elapsed time, a red Stop/Save control, and Pause/Resume.
9. Tap red Stop/Save and let saving finish. Open LIBRARY, play the result, and download important work.

chunks.title: The whole recording flow
chunks.text: The countdown is fixed for each new take; there is no “None” option. Resume continues the same take rather than starting a fresh countdown. Time spent paused is left out of the saved take. Audio playback and live camera activity can continue while the take is paused.

chunks.title: Every control on the RECORD subtab
chunks.text:
| Control | What to do with it |
|---|---|
| RECORD · 3–2–1 | Starts with the current setup after preparation/test and the countdown. |
| TEST OUTPUT | Checks the current video composition load. Test with the real camera/effects enabled; a lighter test does not prove a heavier performance will work. |
| SNAPSHOT | Saves/downloads a PNG of the selected output's current composed picture. Safe guides and recording controls are excluded. It is also listed in Library. |
| PAUSE / RESUME | Temporarily leave time and changes out of the take, then continue. Not the source Play/Pause. |
| STOP & SAVE | Finalizes the current take's files. Wait for the saved message. |
| MARKER | Adds a timestamp marker to the current take. Later it can be tapped to seek in Library. It does not add a visible title to the picture or split the file automatically. |
| Capture | Video recording, or Audio only · WAV. Audio-only captures the mixed WAV and skips the video-rendering performance test. |
| Stop after seconds · 0 = manual | Optional automatic duration cap, up to 14,400 seconds (four hours). It is a maximum setting, not a guarantee that a phone/storage/codec can sustain it. 0 means you stop manually. |
| Record output B at the same time | Records a second independent visual composition. B's preview alone does not enable recording B. This is a second shape/mix of the same live rig, not a second camera or a separate song. |
| Save separate music and microphone WAV files | Saves isolated companion sources before the recorder's gain/mute controls. You may get a silent companion if no corresponding source was active. |
| Also save the mixed audio as a WAV file | Adds a standalone mix WAV alongside video. Audio-only already creates a mix WAV. |

chunks.title: Every control on the RECORD subtab
chunks.text:
| Storage estimate | Approximate free space available to this browser/site, not necessarily the phone's entire disk. |
| PLAY DEMO | Starts the built-in demo through the normal main source routing. It changes the main source; use it intentionally. |
| PROTECT DEVICE STORAGE | Requests persistent browser storage where supported. A grant can reduce automatic eviction; it is not a backup or a promise against manual site-data clearing. |

A video normally includes its chosen audio track; companion WAVs are additional files. A/B videos and music/mic/mix companions appear as separate Library items. Removing one companion does not automatically remove the others.

chunks.title: 17. OUTPUT: decide what the saved picture looks like
chunks.text: OUTPUT A and OUTPUT B each have their own profile. Choose the tab before adjusting values. **A is recorded by default**; **B is preview only until dual recording is enabled**. Both use the same live scene/camera performance but render to their own composition sizes and feedback histories.

chunks.title: Shape, resolution and motion
chunks.text:
| Setting | What it means |
|---|---|
| Platform preset | Sets a starting width/height and approximate preview safe area. It does not connect an account, upload a file or guarantee a platform's current acceptance limits. |
| Width / Height | Custom pixel dimensions. Each must be even and between 128 and 3840; total area cannot exceed 3840 × 2160 pixels. Device limits also apply. |
| Resolution shortcut | 720p for a lighter take, 1080p for more detail, 2160p for permitted desktop configurations. |
| Frame rate | 24, 30 or 60 fps. 60 needs a capable configuration and a successful test; it is not automatic motion smoothing. |
| Output orientation | Landscape, portrait or square composition with upright text at rotation 0°. |
| Rotate entire picture | 0°, 90° clockwise, 180° or 270° clockwise. Rotates the visual **and all recorded overlays/text**. A 90°/270° rotation swaps encoded width/height. |
| Framing | Render for this shape; Fit operator aspect; or Fill from operator aspect. See below. |
| Zoom | 1–2× framing zoom of this output. This is not FORM → ZOOM and does not change both outputs together. |
| Frame left/right; up/down | −1 to +1 positioning of excess image area. If the image already exactly fills that axis, panning there can have little/no visible effect. |
| Fit background | Color behind a letterboxed/pillarboxed fit. It does not replace the scene palette. |

chunks.title: Orientation versus rotation—the part that causes confusion
chunks.text:
**Want a normal landscape video with readable upright words?** Choose Landscape and leave Rotate entire picture at 0°.

**Want a normal vertical phone video?** Choose Portrait and rotation 0°.
